summary: Implemented scripts/preview-prompts.py: standalone Python 3.11+ script with STAGES registry, render_and_write helper, argparse CLI (--stage, --list flags), pathlib.Path throughout, sys.path bootstrap for prompt_renderer import, summary output with ✓ lines.
Added cmdPreviewPrompts function to scripts/cli.js using venvBin('python') + spawnSync with stdio: 'inherit', matching the pattern of other sync commands.
Added preview-prompts COMMANDS entry in Orchestrator category between preflight and orchestrator, with hidden:true, helpVariants for --stage and --list, assigned to cmdPreviewPrompts.
Appended dist/ as a distinct line entry to orchestrator/.gitignore.

Verified: 14 files written on default run; --list prints 8 names exits 0 without file I/O; --stage developer writes 2 files; --stage pm writes 1 file; --stage bogus exits non-zero with error referencing 'bogus'; rendered files contain no literal {project_path}/{wp_id} tokens and no {{#if}}/{{/if}} markers; with-wp/without-wp variants differ; node scripts/cli.js help shows preview-prompts with both variants; no forbidden module imports; all paths via pathlib.Path.

comments.note: orchestrator/.venv uses Python 3.14 which emits a UserWarning about Pydantic V1 incompatibility via langchain_core on every import. The warning originates in an installed dependency (langchain_core), not the new script. It appears even on the --list invocation because sys.path insertion triggers langchain_core's pydantic compatibility check. This is pre-existing technical debt in the dependency stack, not caused by this WP.

scripts/preview-prompts.py: the UserWarning from langchain_core propagates to stderr on every run. A simple warnings.filterwarnings('ignore') at the top of the script could suppress it for cleaner output, but this would mask future legitimate warnings. The correct fix is an upstream dependency upgrade — noted here for awareness.

scripts/cli.js: cmdPreviewPrompts does not call process.exit(result.status) when status is 0 (it exits naturally), but it does forward non-zero exit codes. This is consistent with how other similar inline spawnSync commands in the file behave (e.g. cmdCtxGenerate pattern), so no action required — recorded for completeness.

summary: Code review PASS. All three modified files reviewed against maintainability, best practices, performance, and architectural fit.

scripts/preview-prompts.py: Design is clean and well-structured. STAGES registry as a list-of-dicts is appropriate for this use case — simple, readable, and easily extensible. The _render_stage / render_and_write separation is well-scoped. pathlib.Path throughout; no os.path calls. sys.path bootstrap is a standard and correct pattern for a standalone script that needs to import from the adjacent package without installation. argparse usage is idiomatic. The `from __future__ import annotations` import is correct for Python 3.11+ type hints used in function signatures.

scripts/cli.js — cmdPreviewPrompts: Follows the exact codebase pattern for venvBin-backed sync commands. stdio: 'inherit' correctly forwards all I/O streams to the caller. Non-zero exit forwarding via process.exit(result.status ?? 1) is consistent with cmdCtxGenerate and similar commands. No issues.
orchestrator/.gitignore: dist/ added as a distinct line (line 9). Correct and expected. No issues.

Without-wp template design confirmed intentional: the developer.md template (and peers) gate all WP-specific content in {{#if wp_id}} blocks. Passing wp_id='' for the without-wp render causes those blocks to be stripped, yielding a minimal project_path-only prompt. This is the correct behavior — the sparse output is a template design choice, not a gap.
Fix-Forward applied: trailing double-space inconsistency on the synthesis row in the STAGES registry (line 54) corrected to match all other rows. Non-behavioral whitespace-only change.

comments.note: scripts/preview-prompts.py line 54: synthesis entry had a double-space after 'False,' (i.e., 'False,  "extra_vars"') while all other rows use a single space. Corrected to 'False, "extra_vars"' for consistency. Non-behavioral whitespace-only change — QA validation remains fully intact.

scripts/preview-prompts.py: STAGES is a module-level mutable list of plain dicts (STAGES: list[dict]). In practice nothing mutates it, so this is safe, but annotating it more precisely (e.g. list[dict[str, Any]]) or using a TypedDict/NamedTuple for stage entries would make the contract explicit and catch future accidental mutations. Low priority — the current form is clear enough for a small registry.

scripts/preview-prompts.py: _BASE_VARS is a module-level mutable dict. It is never mutated (render calls use dict unpacking to merge it into a new local dict), so there is no bug — but marking it as effectively constant by convention (e.g. via a comment or by converting to a MappingProxyType) would make the intent clearer for future maintainers.

[documentation-forward] scripts/preview-prompts.py module docstring is thorough but does not document the STAGES registry structure (field names, semantics of wp_scoped/extra_vars) or explain the with-wp/without-wp variant pattern. Adding a brief 'Stage registry format' section to the module docstring — or a comment block above STAGES — would make the extension path obvious to future contributors adding new stages.

[documentation-forward] The orchestrator README (or a CONTRIBUTING note) should mention that scripts/preview-prompts.py / node scripts/cli.js preview-prompts exists as a developer utility for inspecting rendered stage prompts. Currently discoverable only via 'node scripts/cli.js help' — a brief callout in the docs would help onboarding.

No summary line is printed when running in --stage single-stage mode (e.g. '1 file written'). The current output is just the ✓ lines which is fine, but a trailing count line ('1 file(s) written to orchestrator/dist/stage-prompts/') would bring it in line with the default-run UX. Minor DX improvement only — does not affect any AC.
